title: Timezone Converter: Convert a Time Between Zones
description: Convert a local time from one place to another with the Timezone Converter — daylight saving handled, date shifts shown. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 9:00 a.m. Monday in New York is 2:00 p.m. Monday in London but 1:00 a.m. Tuesday in Sydney — one conversion, two kinds of surprise, both shown plainly.
quick_answer: The Timezone Converter converts a local time from one location or zone to another, applying each side's daylight-saving rules for that date. Choose the two places, enter the time, and read the converted result — including the date shift, because half the world's conversions quietly change the day.

“Midnight Pacific” is a specific instant. Convert it to your clock before the calendar writes its own version.
A Friday 5 p.m. deadline in Los Angeles is Saturday 10 a.m. in Sydney. The converter shows the day change in the result because hiding it is how deadlines get missed.
Converting with fixed offsets breaks twice a year. This converter applies the rules for the actual date on both sides — the difference is the whole product.

faq: Yes — each side's rules are applied for the date of the time being converted, which is precisely where fixed-offset converters fail.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — places and zones are chosen by you.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Zone names follow the IANA database; other tools may label zones by city or abbreviation differently while computing the same instant.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — it is never requested here.
